clue.text: A number of people about to go into the theatre

definitions.text: A number of people about to go into the theatre

parts.words: A number of people about to go into the theatre
parts.note: a 'number' read as something that numbs, given to surgical patients before an operation in the operating theatre

explanation.surface: A crowd of playgoers waiting to file into the auditorium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a count of people, but it means a thing that makes you numb, and the 'theatre' is a hospital operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that removes sensation is literally something that numbs, used on patients before surgery.

clue.text: Japanese play the Spanish in season

parts.note: Noh, also spelt No, is classical Japanese masked drama
el is the Spanish word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A Japanese drama involving Spaniards staged at a particular time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is the festive season, often called Noel in carols and cards.

clue.text: Sees trouble, grabs a hat, and gets out

indicators.note: grabs means the rearranged letters take hold of the hat, which sits inside them
to trouble something is to disturb it, so the letters of sees are stirred up

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: Someone spots danger, snatches a cap and flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges the four letters into two pairs of ES, and 'grabs' means those letters close round the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to break free and get away from confinement.

clue.text: Period of time may be spring — but not winter

definitions.meaning: an old sense, kept in words like Yuletide and eventide

definitions.text: may be spring — but not winter
definitions.meaning: the sea's rise and fall comes as a spring or a neap one, never a winter one

explanation.surface: A season can be spring, but apparently winter does not count.
explanation.walkthrough: The seasons are a red herring: 'spring' here is the spring kind of sea movement, which has nothing to do with the time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Tide once meant a season or time, and the ocean's spring flow is one type of sea level change.

clue.text: Clare is making cakes

indicators.note: making suggests the letters of the two words are worked into something new

explanation.surface: A woman called Clare is baking pastries.
explanation.definitionFit: Choux pastries filled with cream and topped with chocolate are a familiar sort of cake.

clue.text: One has an old-fashioned image

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made anew, so the letters of old are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone owns a dated picture or likeness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' reads as one adjective, but it splits: 'old' is the fodder and 'fashioned' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue or figure worshipped as a god is a graven image.

clue.text: Apt to steal

definitions.meaning: to take something for one's own use without permission

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means suitable and the verb means to seize property as one's own; the words are spelt alike but said differently.

clue.text: I called cops out for minor offences

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the three words are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone summoned the police over small misdemeanours.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sins or trivial wrongdoings are known by this Spanish-derived word.

clue.text: They make comebacks, just the same

definitions.text: They make comebacks, just the same

parts.words: They make comebacks, just the same
parts.note: words that, read backwards, come out exactly as they were forwards

explanation.surface: Retired performers keep returning to the stage regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comebacks' suggests returning stars; here it means reading backwards and getting the identical word.
explanation.definitionFit: Such words or phrases, like level or radar, read identically in either direction.

clue.text: Feeling of nausea after feeling swell

definitions.text: Feeling of nausea after feeling swell

parts.words: Feeling of nausea after feeling swell
parts.note: 'swell' is the heaving of the sea, not feeling fine, and the queasiness follows from it

explanation.surface: Ironically feeling sick right after feeling great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like slang for 'great'; it is the rolling motion of the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea brought on by a ship's motion on rough water is the classic sailor's malady.

clue.text: What the unpopular candidate will do?

definitions.text: What the unpopular candidate will do?

parts.words: What the unpopular candidate will do?
parts.note: an election candidate both puts himself forward and is likely to be beaten, so both senses of the phrase fit

explanation.surface: Speculating on the fate of a disliked politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means 'be at risk of losing', and an unpopular candidate literally stands for election and loses.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be likely to suffer a loss, which is the fate awaiting a disliked election hopeful.

clue.text: One way to ring the changes

definitions.text: One way to ring the changes

parts.words: One way to ring the changes
parts.note: the idiom 'ring the changes' means vary things, but literally it is bell-ringing through set sequences

explanation.surface: Advice on how to introduce some variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring the changes' sounds like a call for variety; read literally it is church bell-ringing, where changes are sequences rung on a set of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of bells rung in sequence, or a loud chime of them, is how change-ringing sounds.

clue.text: The opposite of borrowed time

definitions.meaning: given on loan to someone else
the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Borrowed time has an opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of loan is the reverse of borrowed, and the forty days before Easter are a church season.

clue.text: Worked to rule?

parts.note: 'work to rule' is an industrial go-slow, but here the work consists of ruling as a monarch

explanation.surface: Asking whether staff staged a go-slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work to rule' is British industrial action where staff do only the strict minimum; here it means a sovereign's job of ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who held the throne ruled, which is the job a king or queen does.

clue.text: Rich man takes the plunge

definitions.meaning: the traditional name for the rich man in Jesus's parable of Lazarus

explanation.surface: A wealthy man makes a bold commitment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dives is Latin for wealthy, used as the name of the parable's wealthy man, and someone plunging head first into a pool goes diving.

clue.text: I'm held in scorn, turning bright red

indicators.note: held in means one piece is gripped inside the other
turning signals that the letters of scorn are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone held in contempt blushes deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges the letters into CRSON, and 'held in' means the other piece is gripped inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, rich shade of red, the colour of a blush or blood.

clue.text: Part of a car to take one's breath away

definitions.meaning: a valve controlling air to the carburettor in older engines
to stop someone breathing, to strangle or suffocate

explanation.surface: A vehicle component that is breathtaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The air-restricting valve on a carburettor shares its name with the verb meaning to stop the windpipe.

clue.text: Expresses regret for glue that's weak, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word sounding like the one given is wanted

parts.note: size is a thin gelatinous glue used to prime paper or plaster

explanation.surface: Someone laments a feeble adhesive.
explanation.walkthrough: SIZE, a weak glue, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing out audibly with sadness is how one shows sorrow or wistful regret.

clue.text: They're evacuated during the shelling

parts.note: evacuation and shelling sound like war, but the shelling is of peas, emptying their cases

explanation.surface: Civilians removed from a town under bombardment.
explanation.walkthrough: The war picture misleads: shelling peas means emptying them from their husks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea husks are emptied of peas when a cook shells them.

clue.text: Tail trimmed to a point

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
trimmed means cut short

explanation.surface: An animal's tail clipped into a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, upright tail, as on a rabbit or deer, is called by this word.

clue.text: Bills for magistrates and teachers

definitions.meaning: British slang for a justice of the peace and, among schoolchildren, a schoolmaster

explanation.surface: Invoices for the bench and staff room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is old British slang for a magistrate and, in schools, a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's hard mouthpart is its bill, and old slang applied the same word to judges and schoolmasters.

clue.text: Teacher on the job needs support for his retirement

indicators.note: on means placed after, the job following the teacher

parts.note: a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is the teaching degree
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A teacher in work needs a pension when he stops working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' is going to sleep at night, not a pension; 'on' places the job after the teacher, as in down clues one piece sits on another.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring at night means going to bed, and the corner pillar of a bedframe holds it up.

clue.text: The last form of secrecy

indicators.note: form of signals a new shape made from the letters of the words

explanation.surface: The final kind of confidentiality.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting covertly, unseen and unheard, is moving with furtiveness.

clue.text: They provide the subtle humour that is found in clubs

indicators.note: found in signals one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: irons are a type of golf club
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Wry wit circulates in gentlemen's clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' looks like social clubs; they are golf irons.
explanation.definitionFit: Wry humour arises from saying the opposite of what is meant, or from twists of fate.

clue.text: Point learnt afresh, always to be remembered

parts.note: E is east, a compass point

indicators.note: afresh means anew, so the letters of learnt are arranged again

explanation.surface: A lesson relearnt, never to be forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afresh' turns LEARNT into TERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting lasts for ever, so it is never forgotten.

clue.text: Small banks of sand in the river

definitions.meaning: golfers once teed off from small heaps of sand

explanation.surface: Sandbanks seen in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf balls were once set on little mounds of sand to drive; the Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers' starting mounds were once made of sand, and the Tees runs through Teesside to the North Sea.

clue.text: Stiffen a bristle

parts.note: to set is to harden or stiffen

explanation.surface: Bristling, someone tenses up.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology, a stiff hair or bristle-like structure on a worm or insect has this Latin name.

clue.text: Axe broadcast commercials

indicators.note: broadcast signals the word is spoken out, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: ads are advertisements on television or radio

explanation.surface: Scrap the broadcast adverts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axe' looks like a verb, 'cancel'; it is a noun, the tool. ADS sounds like it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting tool with an arched blade at right angles to its handle, a kind of woodworking chopper.

clue.text: One vessel accommodates one rowing crew

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: accommodates means the vessel houses something inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
again the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A boat carrying one oarsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Isis is the Oxford University reserve boat in the Boat Race, named after the stretch of the Thames at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford second eight that races Cambridge's reserves bears this name.

clue.text: Land in the water

parts.note: 'land' looks like a verb, as of a plane ditching, but it is a noun: ground surrounded by sea

explanation.surface: Make a landing at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'land' as a noun: a piece of ground with water all round.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a stretch of ground surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Form II is not the best

definitions.meaning: a school form is a class, so the second form

explanation.surface: Year two at school is not the top.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a 'form' is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-year school group, and also anything ranked below first rate or of lesser quality.

clue.text: His depredations affect the stockholder

parts.note: a stockholder looks like a shareholder, but here it is a farmer holding livestock

explanation.surface: A fraudster's plundering hurts investors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stockholder' suggests finance; read it as someone who keeps livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals herds of livestock from farmers.
